references.text: Hobab was the son-in-law of Moses, and this text describes Moses' first meeting with Jethro's family in Midian, which established the family bond.
Jethro, Hobab's father, gave advice to Moses on how he should lead the people. Hobab's knowledge of the desert would be valuable in a similar way.
The Kenites, descendants of Moses' father-in-law, settled in Israel, suggesting that Hobab or his family eventually joined the Israelites.
Heber the Kenite was a descendant of Hobab, Moses' father-in-law, showing that Hobab's family remained connected to Israel.
The Kenites showed kindness to the Israelites when they came out of Egypt, which may be linked to Hobab's role as a guide in the desert.
The expression 'to be eyes for' describes guidance and leadership, just as Moses asked Hobab to be for the Israelites in the desert.
Job describes himself as 'eyes for the blind,' using the same metaphor that Moses used to describe Hobab's role as a guide.
